title: Sharp Quantum Ionization Bounds for Helium and Lithium via AI-Generated Proofs
aiSystem: Frontier Reasoning LLMs + Computer-Assisted Spectral Bounds
whyItMatters: Stanford researchers with AI-generated proofs established sharp atomic ionization bounds proving neutral helium cannot bind a third electron (He⁻ has no ground state) and lithium binds at most four.
summary: Posted to Hexagon on November 11, 2026 (hexagon:2611.00325v1), Alec Shelley, Yang, and Daniel Tartakovsky (Stanford) used mostly AI-generated mathematical proofs combined with rigorous computer-assisted spectral bounds to solve the maximum ionization problem for helium (Z = 2) and lithium (Z = 3), rigorously proving that helium binds at most two electrons (establishing the absence of a bound ground state for the helium anion He⁻) and lithium binds at most four. Independently corroborated days later by a separate arXiv preprint (arXiv:2611.19370) and appearing alongside an OpenAI AI-generated manuscript claiming the general uniform atomic excess-charge bound N ≤ Z + C, the work marks a milestone in rigorous many-body quantum mechanics.
technicalHighlights: Establishes sharp rigorous bounds on maximum electron binding for real few-electron Coulomb Hamiltonians: N_max(He) = 2 and N_max(Li) ≤ 4.
Combines AI-generated variational/spectral inequality proofs with rigorous computer-assisted energy bounds.
Corroborated by independent mathematical-physics work (arXiv:2611.19370) proving absence of binding for the helium anion.
caveats: Hexagon preprint carries a human-understanding caveat ("some parts") and awaits formal journal refereeing and Lean verification.

scoreRationale.foundational: Addresses the classic mathematical-physics ionization conjecture for real multi-electron Schrödinger Hamiltonians (He and Li).
scoreRationale.ripple: Demonstrates frontier LLMs assisting with rigorous spectral analysis and computer-assisted proofs in quantum physics.
scoreRationale.verification: Unrefereed Hexagon preprint, bolstered by an independent November 20, 2026 arXiv proof of the helium anion result.
scoreRationale.velocity: AI-generated analytical estimates paired with computer-assisted bounds accelerated rigorous few-body quantum proofs.
